In a recent development, transactional emails are easy to overlook during application development. A registration form works, the database stores the user's information, and the backend successfully triggers an email. Everything appears to be functioning as expected.

Then a user reports that their password-reset message never arrived.

Industry observers note that the problem might not be in the email template or the sending function. It could involve DNS configuration, authentication failures, message formatting, queue processing, recipient-server policies, or an incorrectly configured production environment.

For developers building SaaS applications, ecommerce platforms, and web services, reliable email delivery is an notable part of the user experience. An account-verification message that never arrives can prevent someone from accessing an application, while a delayed security notification can create unnecessary confusion.

Understanding how to investigate these problems requires looking beyond the email-sending function. This guide explores a practical debugging workflow, the technical layers involved, and the tools developers can use to identify common email delivery failures.

One of the first mistakes developers make when troubleshooting email is assuming that a successful API response means the message has reached the recipient.

These are two different events.

When an application submits an email through an SMTP server or an email service provider's API, the provider may accept the request and return a successful response. However, the receiving mail server still needs to process the message.

Depending on its configuration and policies, the receiving server might:.

Accept the message and place it in the inbox.

Accept the message but classify it as spam.

Reject the message because of authentication or policy issues.

Accept the message but place it in another folder.

A successful request therefore confirms only that a particular stage of the process completed.

Developers should distinguish between three key states:.

Submission: The application successfully handed the message to its sending provider.

Acceptance: The receiving mail server accepted responsibility for the message.

Inbox placement: The message became visible in the recipient's expected inbox.

These distinctions make troubleshooting considerably easier. Instead of immediately rewriting an email template, developers can identify which stage is actually failing.

Before investigating external email infrastructure, examine the application's own implementation.

Industry observers note that A common example is a password-reset workflow. The application receives a request, generates a temporary token, creates a reset URL, and sends an email containing that URL.

Several problems can occur before the message even reaches an email provider.

The application generates an expired token.

The reset URL points to a staging environment.

An asynchronous task fails before processing the message.

The email service credentials are incorrect.

An API request times out without being retried.

The application records success before confirming the provider's response.

Start by logging the vital stages of the process.

For example, a Node.js application might use structured logging:.

Recent findings suggest that this example assumes that the email provider returns a message identifier. Adapt the response fields to the actual SDK being used.

Notice that the logs identify the recipient through an internal ID rather than exposing their complete email address.

Avoid logging passwords, authentication tokens, reset URLs, or other sensitive information.

The objective is to establish a traceable record of what happened without introducing additional security risks.

Email authentication is another vital area to investigate when messages are rejected or consistently classified as spam.

Three commonly used mechanisms help receiving servers evaluate whether a message is authorized to represent a particular domain.

Sender Policy Framework (SPF) allows a domain owner to specify which servers are authorized to send messages using that domain.

This information is published through DNS.

A simplified SPF record might look like this:.

The actual record must reflect the sending services authorized by the domain owner.

Common configuration mistakes include:.

Forgetting to authorize a latest email provider.

Publishing multiple SPF records for the same domain.

Exceeding SPF's DNS lookup limit.

Leaving outdated sending services in the record.

Sources indicate that remember that SPF evaluates the sending infrastructure against the envelope sender domain. It does not automatically guarantee that the visible From address is aligned.

DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing messages.

The receiving server can retrieve the corresponding public key through DNS and verify that the signature is valid.

A failed DKIM check might indicate:.

A mismatch between the configured selector and published record.

Message modification after signing.

Developers integrating multiple email providers should verify that each provider has the correct signing configuration.

Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) builds on SPF and DKIM.

It allows domain owners to define how receiving servers should handle messages that fail authentication and alignment requirements.

A basic monitoring-oriented DMARC record might look like this:.

It has been revealed that this is an illustrative configuration. The reporting address must be valid, and the domain should have an appropriate monitoring and policy-enforcement initiative.

Developers can use MXToolbox to inspect DNS records and investigate common authentication problems.

For additional technical background, SitePoint's guide to HTML email development explains why email environments require different implementation considerations from ordinary web pages.

An email template that looks perfect in a browser can behave differently when rendered by Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, or another email client.

This happens because email clients do not implement HTML and CSS in exactly the same way.

A layout may break because of unsupported CSS properties, image restrictions, unexpected font rendering, or differences in how tables are handled.

For this reason, email testing should be part of the development process rather than something performed only after users report a problem.

A useful testing sequence includes:.

HTML validation: Check the markup for malformed elements, missing attributes, and unnecessary code.

Rendering tests: Preview the email across desktop and mobile email clients.

Link verification: Confirm that buttons, links, and personalized URLs point to the correct destinations.

Image testing: Check whether the message remains understandable when images are blocked.

Content inspection: Review subject lines, sender information, and the plain-text alternative.

Deliverability checks: Examine authentication, content-related warnings, and potential inbox placement problems.

Developers can also incorporate pre-send diagnostics into their release workflow to identify potential deliverability problems before a message is sent to a larger audience.

The important point is to treat these checks as one part of quality assurance, not as a guarantee that every message will reach the primary inbox.

For more information about email rendering differences, SitePoint's article on essential HTML email coding tips provides useful examples of client-specific behavior.

Testing transactional emails with real customer addresses during development can create unnecessary problems.

A better approach is to use a dedicated testing environment that captures outgoing messages without delivering them to actual recipients.

For example, Mailpit provides a local SMTP server and web interface for inspecting messages during development.

It allows developers to examine:.

Email subject lines and headers.

Embedded images and attachments.

The final output generated by the application.

Another option is Mailtrap, which provides email testing capabilities for development workflows.

Consider a registration feature that sends a welcome message whenever a new user creates an account.

Instead of sending hundreds of test messages to real addresses, developers can configure the development environment to capture them in a testing inbox.

This makes it possible to repeatedly test different templates without affecting actual customers or generating unnecessary email traffic.

A separate testing environment also reduces the risk of accidentally sending development notifications to production users.

Applications that send large numbers of emails often use background workers instead of processing every message during the original HTTP request.

This approach helps keep the application responsive, but it introduces another potential source of failures.

Imagine an ecommerce application that sends order confirmations after checkout.

Sources indicate that the application creates an order successfully and places an email task in a queue. However, the background worker becomes unavailable before processing the task.

The customer receives an order confirmation much later than expected, or perhaps not at all.

To investigate these problems, developers should monitor:.

Retries are particularly key, but they need to be implemented carefully.

A temporary network failure may justify another attempt. A permanent rejection caused by an invalid recipient address usually does not.

Exponential backoff can help prevent repeated requests from overwhelming an unavailable service.

In a production system, add random jitter to avoid having multiple workers retry simultaneously.

Also consider idempotency. If a worker processes the same task twice, the application should avoid sending duplicate transactional messages whenever possible.

A reliable queue architecture should distinguish between temporary failures and permanent failures rather than retrying every error indefinitely.

Testing before deployment is important, but it cannot reveal every glitch that may occur in production.

Real email traffic introduces changing conditions, including recipient-server behavior, sender reputation, invalid addresses, and differences between email providers.

Developers should therefore establish ongoing monitoring.

For Gmail-related monitoring, Google Postmaster Tools provides information about domain reputation, spam rates, and authentication.

It is particularly useful for teams sending enough email to generate meaningful reporting data.

Another useful resource is Can I Email, which documents HTML and CSS feature support across email clients.

These tools address different problems. Monitoring sender reputation will not fix a broken password-reset URL, just as validating HTML will not resolve a DNS authentication failure.

The best approach is to monitor each layer independently.

A repeatable checklist helps developers investigate problems without overlooking vital details.

Before releasing a newly introduced email feature, review the following:.

Confirm that the application successfully submits the message.

Verify that provider credentials and environment variables are correct.

Check the SMTP or API response.

Inspect SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration.

Validate the HTML and plain-text versions.

Test links and personalized content.

Preview the message on desktop and mobile email clients.

Verify that development and production configurations are separated.

Test queue failures and retry behavior.

Check delivery events and provider error reports.

Monitor bounce and complaint rates after deployment.

Not every application needs an expensive testing platform or a complicated monitoring stack.

A small project might only require a local email testing environment, basic DNS checks, and structured application logs.

A larger SaaS platform may benefit from automated integration tests, provider webhooks, queue monitoring, authentication reports, and dedicated deliverability testing.

The right setup depends on the application's sending volume, complexity, and the importance of its email workflows.

Reliable email delivery requires more than calling an SMTP function or integrating an email API.

Developers need to understand the complete process, from application logic and message construction to authentication, queue processing, recipient-server acceptance, and inbox placement.

The most effective troubleshooting strategy is to isolate these layers instead of treating every missing message as a template problem.

Start with application logs, inspect provider responses, validate authentication records, test email rendering, and monitor production behavior.

By incorporating these checks into development and deployment workflows, teams can reduce avoidable failures and build applications that communicate more reliably with their consumers.

Industry News: SSDs, laptops, and phones may get cheaper as consumer NAND spot pricing drops 20%

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that solid-state drives, phones, laptops, and tablets have all gotten substantially pricier in the last couple of years.
  • According to recent reports, the report observes a 20% drop in spot pricing for NAND chips over just the last month.
  • SED notes that according to that note, 512 Gb NAND wafers saw a 32% drop to $14.30 apiece on the spot market, while 1 Tb wafers fell 19% to $24.90.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that solid-state drives, phones, laptops, and tablets have all gotten substantially pricier in the last couple of years. Beyond the stratospheric prices of DDR5 memory, prospective PC builders and consumer electronics buyers have had to deal with upcharges on SSDs of all sizes thanks to the AI boom. That may be changing soon, as spot pricing for consumer NAND chips is reportedly dropping, according to a newly introduced report from Seoul Economic Daily (SED).

According to recent reports, the report observes a 20% drop in spot pricing for NAND chips over just the last month. Its conclusions are bolstered by information from a Bank of America note from Nov. 13, wherein industry sources tell that institution that NAND is due for a market correction.

SED notes that according to that note, 512 Gb NAND wafers saw a 32% drop to $14.30 apiece on the spot market, while 1 Tb wafers fell 19% to $24.90. SED quotes another industry source that says: "NAND cannot sustain the steep price gains seen so far.".

It has been revealed that those decreases may be hard to square in a time when enterprise SSDs are getting pricier by the day, but SED notes that the rise in phone and PC prices has led customers to delay upgrades, resulting in a 20% year-on-year decline in shipments for phones alone and making for the lowest third-quarter volumes in 14 years. Meanwhile, PC shipments have also fallen 22.5% year-on-year, according to a Gartner report.

In the face of those consumer decisions, device makers are letting their existing stock drain out and are presumably stocked with NAND chips for the short term, thus resulting in lower prices for upcoming fab shipments on the short-term spot market.

Another factor in the consumer NAND market is that not all flash is equal. Both RAM and NAND makers have been redirecting their chip output to serve the ongoing AI boom, converting their consumer-grade production lines to make higher-spec silicon. Memory factories have been converting DDR5 capacity to HBM at a steady pace, as parts of the process are shared across both types.

But according to the Bank of America note that SED cites, things are different in the NAND world. High-density flash now sits at around 300 layers, and its production requires substantially different tooling compared to the lower-grade silicon deemed suitable for us mere mortals. So the continuing growth in NAND demand from AI data centers may not translate directly into reduced consumer supply.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, beyond those factors, added supply from Chinese NAND maker YMTC is creating additional downward price pressure in the NAND market. SED notes that YMTC has taken a 14% chunk from major players in the NAND market in the second quarter of this year alone.

On net, these forces could result in a bit of relief for consumer tech. SED states Bank of America expects consumer NAND prices for PCs and smartphones to fall 5% to 10% on the longer-term contract market in the first quarter of 2027, while enterprise NAND contract prices are expected to hold more or less steady.

In a recent development, whether those declines translate to lower prices for finished devices and components like SSDs will remain to be seen, and products with those chips inside will require some time to reach the market. But in the ongoing AI supply crunch, any potential relief is worth celebrating.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA has confirmed that Voyager 1 is the first human-made object to reach one light-day's distance from Earth, passing the milestone today.
  • According to recent reports, there are many astronomical numbers behind what is an extraordinary feat.
  • These are probably bigger distances than you are used to fathoming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA has confirmed that Voyager 1 is the first human-made object to reach one light-day's distance from Earth, passing the milestone today. A countdown at Orbital Radar confirmed that Voyager cruised past the threshold at a leisurely 37,844 mph just after 5 am ET on Wednesday, November 18. It means that Voyager is now more than 16 billion miles away, and that a signal from the spacecraft now takes fully 24 hours to travel the distance.

According to recent reports, there are many astronomical numbers behind what is an extraordinary feat. Sci-fi reveals casually mention light-years as if they are like a trip to the local convenience store. One light-day isn’t a distance to be derided, though. Over the last half century, hurtling through space at a cruising speed of 38,000 mph, the Voyager spacecraft has clocked about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers).

These are probably bigger distances than you are used to fathoming. So NASA has kindly provided some context with the distances of various heavenly bodies in miles and light-speeds. For example, the Moon is 238,855 miles distant, or about 1.3 light seconds away from Earth. Due to Mars’ independent orbit around the Sun, it can take between three minutes and 22 minutes for light to travel between the red and the blue planet. Meanwhile, the Sun’s rays reach Earth, about 93 million miles away, in 20 light seconds. Now let us remind you that Voyager 1 is on the brink of being a whole light-day away.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, with this major milestone passed, Voyager 1’s journey will be far from over. NASA says that it is on course for an obscure star called Gliese 445, now in the constellation Ursa Minor. We’ll have to keep the champagne on ice for another 40,000 years to celebrate the fly-past of that star, though.

Voyager 1 carries a copy of the Golden Record. Like sending a message in a bottle, NASA scientists released Voyager with the hope that someone, somewhere will eventually read the message. Moreover, the receiving aliens will need to source tech to play the record, which contains sounds, music, and the data needed to reconstruct photos that showcase the diversity of life and culture on our planet.

If an alien got hold of the record on Wednesday and managed to rustle up a gramophone player to listen to it, a message sent to Earth via radio waves would take a full 24 hours to be received.

Recent findings suggest that space enthusiasts are also invited to participate in a global event “by creating a wave of golden light.” It sounds rather pointless, but enthusiasts are asked to flash the three-letter call sign for NASA's Voyager mission, VGR, into the night sky - Morse Code style - using their phone flashlights. There’s a website you can open to flash your screen appropriately.

#34664. What Actually Happens When a Kafka Region Fails?

What Actually Happens When a Kafka Region Fails?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Most Kafka deployments in the industry plan to survive the loss of a single Kafka broker or an availability zone.
  • In such scenarios, the failure model should consider not just the loss of a broker or a zone, but the loss of an entire region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Most Kafka deployments in the industry plan to survive the loss of a single Kafka broker or an availability zone. But that's not enough for critical Tier-0 infrastructure where downtime or data loss of even a few seconds could have a massive business impact.

In such scenarios, the failure model should consider not just the loss of a broker or a zone, but the loss of an entire region. The business is expected to operate without interruption even when a whole region goes down, and it should be possible to also roll the cluster safely while operating in that state, to apply any break-glass changes.

It has been revealed that but what actually happens inside Kafka when an entire region goes down? What happens to the replicas, producer writes, and KRaft quorum? And what happens when that region comes back?

Let's walk through these scenarios using a Tier-0 multi-region Kafka architecture.

For a Tier-0 multi-region Kafka cluster, we need three different regions with isolated failure domains and a minimum of two brokers in each region.

Brokers in each region should be configured with rack awareness to indicate their failure domains as follows:.

It has been revealed that for Tier-0 workloads, each topic's partitions should be configured to have a replication factor (RF) of 6. Kafka's rack-aware replica assignment will spread the replicas across the three regions. If the automatic replica assignment doesn't allocate two replicas per region, we have to explicitly reassign replicas immediately after topic creation to meet our availability guarantees.

This way, if one region goes down entirely, we still have four replicas surviving and the cluster would still continue to operate.

But just running brokers in multiple regions is not the solution here. In fact, that's the easy part. The hard question is, what guarantee remains when one of those regions disappears, and does it solve the business needs?

Let's say Region A goes down entirely.

The two brokers in that region become unavailable, leaving four surviving replicas across Regions B and C.

For any partitions whose leaders were in Region A, Kafka needs to elect latest leaders from the surviving in-sync replicas.

But having four surviving replicas alone does not determine whether Kafka will continue accepting writes.

The next step is to define what is considered a successful write in this Kafka setup. For this, we need two configs:.

min.insync.replicas determines the minimum number of replicas that should be present in the in-sync replica set (ISR) of a partition for Kafka to accept writes when producers use acks=all.

acks=all is a producer-side config that ensures that the producer will get an acknowledgment only when the write has been successfully replicated to the required in-sync replicas.

These two settings work together to satisfy the durability guarantees we want.

In a recent development, when all three regions are healthy, ISR would include all six replicas. Let's say one region goes down, then the ISR would drop down to four.

Since minISR is three, writes will still continue to work.

There may be temporary interruptions while Kafka detects the failure, elects new leaders, and clients reconnect to them. But once the surviving leaders are available, the cluster can continue accepting writes as long as the ISR requirements are met.

The goal isn't availability at any cost, but rather the system should be available as long as the durability guarantees that we designed for can be maintained.

Now let's make the scenario more interesting.

Region A is still down. We have four replicas surviving across Regions B and C.

What if we need to roll the cluster one broker at a time, to apply any break-glass changes?

During that time, the ISR can go down from four to three. But since minISR is three, writes will still continue to work.

Let's look at how the cluster behaves under different failure scenarios.

Kafka will stop accepting writes only when the surviving ISR drops below three.

This is an crucial distinction for Tier-0 workloads.

Sources indicate that it's not sufficient to design a cluster that survives a region failure. We also need to consider whether the cluster can continue operating safely while already in that degraded state.

It has been revealed that so far, we focused on the data plane. Now switching gears, the KRaft controllers have a completely different availability model.

They form the metadata quorum, and a majority is needed to continue operation.

For our setup, five controllers could be distributed as 2 + 2 + 1 across the three regions, requiring a majority of three to maintain quorum.

If either of the regions containing two controllers goes down, three controllers remain. If the region containing one controller goes down, four remain.

So, the controller quorum survives the loss of any one region.

But, unlike brokers, we cannot necessarily roll the controllers at that point because taking one controller down could cause the quorum to drop below three.

With a static quorum, one way to solve this is to use more controllers, and a 3 + 3 + 3 distribution would provide this. Losing one region would leave six controllers with room to still roll the controllers, as we only need five to maintain quorum.

It has been revealed that on the flip side, an increase in quorum size also increases the coordination overhead. The official Kafka documentation typically recommends three or five controllers, which tolerate one or two concurrent failures respectively.

Alternatively, with dynamic KRaft quorum (KIP-853), introduced in Kafka 3.9, we can add or remove controllers from the voting quorum without restarting the cluster.

In a recent development, for example, with our 2 + 2 + 1 setup, if a region containing two controllers goes down, the remaining three controllers can still maintain quorum. We can then remove the failed controllers from the voting membership, one at a time, reducing the quorum size to three. This allows us to roll one of the surviving controllers while still maintaining the new majority of two.

It has been revealed that however, dynamic quorum reconfiguration is not automatic. The surviving controllers must be able to maintain quorum and successfully commit the membership changes before we can proceed with the controller restart.

You need to consider whether you want the same availability guarantee for the controllers as that of the data plane, and whether dynamic quorum reconfiguration during a regional outage is acceptable for your Tier-0 workloads.

So far, we assumed that a region either works or goes down completely.

But the WAN itself becomes a failure mode.

In this setup, a partly working WAN between two regions can be more dangerous than a link that's completely down.

Increased latency, packet loss, or intermittent connectivity complications between regions can cause replication to lag, ultimately resulting in replicas falling out of ISR.

The three regions might be independently healthy, but if the connectivity between them is not, then the availability of the cluster might be impacted.

Going back to the CAP theorem, to tolerate a network partition, we must choose between consistency and availability.

So, if a partition's ISR falls below the configured min.insync.replicas of three due to a network partition, Kafka stops accepting writes with acks=all rather than weakening those guarantees.

Similarly, if the KRaft controller quorum is lost, then no metadata changes, like leader elections, can happen in the cluster, even though existing data-plane traffic may continue for some time.

The availability guarantees we discussed also come with their own costs.

The first cost is client latency. With cross-region replication and acks=all, the network latency between these regions directly affects producer latency. Consumers can also pay the WAN latency cost when consuming from partition leaders located in a different region.

The second cost is replication overhead. With RF=6, there is additional storage, network traffic, and replication-related coordination cost in the brokers compared to a smaller number of replicas.

So, in an architecture like this, monitoring the health of the network paths between these regions is as critical as monitoring the Kafka brokers and controllers.

Metrics like round-trip latency (RTT) between regions, packet loss, TCP retransmissions, connection errors/timeouts, and network throughput/bandwidth utilization are a good start.

When one region goes down, all the partition leaders in that region would move to the two other surviving regions.

This implies that those two regions would have to handle more producer and consumer traffic, network throughput, and disk I/O.

Even if the cluster is designed to satisfy its ISR and controller quorum requirements, if it's not sized to handle these failures when one region goes down, the surviving regions would be overloaded, resulting in higher latencies, timeouts, and operational instability.

So, for Tier-0 infrastructure, capacity planning should always be done for failure states and not stop at normal operations.

Now let's say Region A comes back online.

The brokers in the recovered region might have to catch up on a significant amount of data before they become fully in sync again.

This can result in a sudden burst of cross-region network traffic and disk I/O across all regions.

Region recovery needs to be controlled so that it doesn't overwhelm the healthy part of the cluster.

This can be achieved by throttling the replica catch-up, with the trade-off of longer recovery time to minimize the impact on live production traffic.

Replication throttling needs a deeper discussion of its own, so we won't go into details here.

The notable point is that bringing a failed region back online is not simply a matter of restarting its brokers. We need to make sure that the recovery process itself doesn't impact the business.

Before putting a Tier-0 multi-region Kafka cluster into production, validate these scenarios:.

In a recent development, there is no shortage of ways to deploy Kafka across multiple regions. The challenge here is to pick the right architecture that addresses all our durability guarantees.

For Tier-0 workloads, this means designing the architecture around failures first.

In a recent development, what happens when a region goes down? Can we still roll the cluster? What continues to work, and at what point do we deliberately stop accepting writes?

Lastly, can we safely bring back the region that was down without impacting the business?

That is ultimately the difference between simply running Kafka across multiple regions versus actually supporting a mission-critical Tier-0 workload.

  • Industry observers note that A new device on Kickstarter claims to make Game Boy cartridges relevant again by playing soundtracks from your favorite classic Nintendo games.
  • Sources indicate that the Retro Song Bird also comes with a 3.5mm stereo line-out and a USB Type-C port in case you want to connect to other audio equipment.
  • In addition to playing retro video game soundtracks, the Retro Song Bird also supports the Game Boy Camera, allowing you to use it as a webcam offering a glorious 128×112 pixels resolution and 5 frames per second speed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A new device on Kickstarter claims to make Game Boy cartridges relevant again by playing soundtracks from your favorite classic Nintendo games. The Retro Song Bird is a box-shaped speaker that supports Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges, with support for over 1,900 games. Simply inserting a cartridge into the speaker gives you access to all soundtracks and sound effects, which can be controlled using onboard physical controls including next, previous, and volume.

Sources indicate that the Retro Song Bird also comes with a 3.5mm stereo line-out and a USB Type-C port in case you want to connect to other audio equipment. According to the developer, it offers accurate, register-level sound emulation and can be used to sample and remix music from your Game Boy cartridges. It exposes all four audio channels (two square, wave, noise) as separate USB audio streams that can be imported into a DAW. This allows you to isolate individual melodies, waveforms, and sound effects from old games to create your own melodies. There’s even support for LSDj for playing saved chiptune tracks, while two Retro Song Bird units can be synced for DJ-style performances using Game Boy cartridges instead of traditional records.

In addition to playing retro video game soundtracks, the Retro Song Bird also supports the Game Boy Camera, allowing you to use it as a webcam offering a glorious 128×112 pixels resolution and 5 frames per second speed. Other features include the ability to back up and restore save files, ROMs, flash writable carts, and export any soundtrack or sound effect as WAV onto your PC. The listing also includes other abilities, including an Alarm Mode, a record of every cartridge you've ever plugged in, an open API for developers, and over-the-air updates.

Recent findings suggest that the Retro Song Bird is currently available to back on Kickstarter, with the standard model starting at $79. The introductory $59 Early Bird offer has already sold out, while the developer is also offering a two-unit bundle for $150. Shipments are expected to begin in April 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the developer notes that only a handful of hand-assembled prototypes presently exist and that the hardware and design still need some refinements. The project also faces potential manufacturing challenges, including component availability, finding suitable manufacturing partners, and producing injection-molded enclosures. Like any other Kickstarter campaign, delivery timelines are subject to change, and backers should be aware that there is no guarantee the finished product will ship as planned.

Nvidia's revenue hits $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin generates $20 billion in another record-setting quarter

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for the first time in its 33-year history, Nvidia on Tuesday reported quarterly financial results without Jensen Huang at its helm or on the call, after its cofounder and longtime chief executive departed five days ago.
  • According to recent reports, "Our momentum is real.
  • In a recent development, for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended on October 25, 2026, Nvidia posted revenue of $115.844 billion, an increase of 20% sequentially and 103% year-over-year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for the first time in its 33-year history, Nvidia on Tuesday reported quarterly financial results without Jensen Huang at its helm or on the call, after its cofounder and longtime chief executive departed five days ago. To no one's surprise, Nvidia continues to set new financial records as demand for its AI accelerators shows no signs of slowing down. The tech giant reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter of its fiscal 2027, with its latest Vera Rubin platform generating $20 billion. Meanwhile, its supply commitments surged to $390 billion.

According to recent reports, "Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," remarked Colette Kress, interim chief executive and chief financial officer of Nvidia. "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.".

In a recent development, for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended on October 25, 2026, Nvidia posted revenue of $115.844 billion, an increase of 20% sequentially and 103% year-over-year. The manufacturer's net income reached $65.287 billion, up 105% from the same quarter last year, while gross margin hit 74.8%. Revenue from the Compute & Networking segment totaled $106 billion, up 20% quarter-over-quarter and 108% year-over-year. Meanwhile, the Graphics segment generated $9.8 billion, a sequential increase of 25% and 62% compared with the same period a year ago.

According to recent reports, as expected, Nvidia's results during the quarter were primarily driven by its Data Center business, which generated $107.6 billion in revenue (and accounted for approximately 93% of the company's sales), up 21% sequentially and 110% YoY. Hyperscale customers accounted for $60.1 billion, an increase of 23% QoQ and 71% YoY, while sales to AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise customers reached $47.5 billion, up 18% sequentially and 195% compared to the same period last year. Although hyperscalers remain Nvidia's largest customer category, demand from AI cloud providers, industrial companies, and enterprises continues to grow considerably faster on an annual basis. Meanwhile, Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 14% sequentially and 42% year-over-year.

Recent findings suggest that one of the main contributors to Nvidia's growth was its Vera Rubin platform, which generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments, which Nvidia described as the fastest product ramp in its history. The company also reported strong demand for standalone Vera CPUs and continued sales growth for Blackwell Ultra. According to Nvidia, its hyperscale partners brought Vera Rubin systems into production in approximately one month, which is two times faster than the previous-generation Grace Blackwell platform.

"Vera Rubin is off to an extraordinary start: in its first quarter of production shipments, the Rubin platform generated nearly $20 billion in revenue, making it the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history," Kress said. "We continue to see very strong demand for Vera and expect total CPU revenue to more than double in FY2028.".

To support the expected growth of its AI infrastructure business, Nvidia has substantially increased its long-term procurement obligations. The company's supply and capacity commitments reached $390 billion at the end of Q3 FY2027, compared with $279 billion three months earlier and $119 billion at the end of Q1. Nvidia attributed the latest increase primarily to multiyear memory procurement agreements.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, the company expects to fulfill $69 billion of these commitments during the remainder of FY2027 (which ends in late January), followed by $203 billion in FY2028 and $92 billion in FY2029. Another $26 billion is scheduled for FY2030 and beyond. In other words, Nvidia has already committed to purchasing $390 billion worth of components and manufacturing capacity through the end of FY2030, though given the fact that its purchases in FY2028 are set to exceed $200 billion, expect its procurements in FY2030 to be higher.

Industry observers note that the commitments reflect Nvidia's efforts to ensure that its suppliers can manufacture sufficient quantities of advanced processors, memory, substrates, and packaging components. In addition to its existing agreements with partners like TSMC, Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix, Nvidia on Wednesday revealed new partnerships with Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Kinsus for substrates, as well as SPIL for advanced packaging. In addition, the tech giant disclosed agreements with Amkor, Ibiden, KYEC, and Unimicron.

During the earnings call, Kress mentioned that demand for Nvidia's products continues to exceed available supply, prompting the company to work with manufacturing partners to expand production capacity. She also indicated that Nvidia could provide suppliers with prepayments or other financial assistance to accelerate capacity expansion.

In a recent development, although these procurement commitments are gargantuan, Nvidia expects demand for its AI infrastructure to remain strong, which will justify the expenditures. The tech giant raised its revenue growth forecast for FY2028 from approximately 70% to 75% due to stronger demand and additional manufacturing capacity that it expects to secure.

In addition to its supply commitments, Nvidia disclosed $32 billion in agreements with neocloud providers that allow it to earn revenue from hardware sales and participate in cloud rental revenue above a guaranteed minimum. Meanwhile, the manufacturer's maximum financial exposure under various guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support for the PORTS-Pike AI data center campus in Ohio, which will serve OpenAI under 20-year leases.

In total, Nvidia's commitments reached $540 billion as of early Q4 FY2024.

Nvidia presently absorbs higher component and manufacturing costs to honor existing purchase orders and maintain previously agreed prices for its customers. As a result, the firm expects its GAAP gross margin to decline from 74.8% in Q3 FY2027 to 71% – 72% in Q4, which it considers the bottom of the current margin cycle.

Going forward, Nvidia intends to introduce revised pricing in FY2028 to help offset higher supply costs and restore profitability, which is when the firm expects gross margins to recover to 72% – 73% next fiscal year, although it has not disclosed the magnitude of its planned price adjustments or the products they will affect.

In a recent development, "We thought about in terms of our prices and pieces of that, and a lot of the costs were some of the things that we absorbed in those numbers that we included," Kress stated. "What we provided here in Q4 is our bottom. If you recall, that was our bottom as we honored many of the different POs that we had already received from our customers, and we just wanted to make sure that was held solid as we moved to a upcoming pricing, as we moved into the new year.".

In a recent development, perhaps more importantly is that Colette Kress largely sidestepped the question about custom AI accelerators and their potential impact on Nvidia's pricing power. During the conference call, an analyst asked whether Nvidia would accept lower margins to protect its market share against custom AI accelerators developed by hyperscalers. The interim CEO avoided directly addressing whether competition from custom silicon could undermine Nvidia’s competitive position, leaving considerable room for speculation.

Recent findings suggest that for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, Nvidia projects revenue of approximately $130 billion ±3%, which would represent an increase of about 12% sequentially. The organization expects GAAP gross margin of 71% to 72% and GAAP operating expenses of approximately $11 billion during the quarter. Nvidia’s forecast excludes Data Center compute revenue from China and accounts for an additional week in the quarter. While Nvidia expects its gross margin to decline during the Vera Rubin transition, Kress said that the company anticipates a recovery to 72% – 73% in FY2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that even though Nvidia states that it does not plan to bring its former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, that hasn't stopped some of its board members from continuing to lobby for his return. Following the news that some of Huang's allies have formed a "war room" to drive his reinstatement just days after his resignation, one Nvidia employee went so far as to warn that the company faces the possibility of an exodus of "irreplaceable talent" if Huang isn't reinstated. We've even seen U.S. President Trump argue for giving Huang his old job back, but the company said during its November 17 earnings call that wasn't in the cards. Now, Semafor reports that some Nvidia board members aren't taking "no" for an answer.

Huang, for his part, has already said that he would be "honored" to return to the organization that he resigned from in disgrace just a few days ago. At the time, he admitted to having an affair with a woman who worked for Megaspeed, a controversial Nvidia customer linked to the smuggling of export-controlled AI hardware into China. That woman has also been accused of being a Chinese spy, further complicating an already troublesome matter for Nvidia and Huang. Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will make an appearance before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December and are likely to face some difficult questions.

According to recent reports, but despite all of this, Huang is stated to have spoken with at least one Nvidia board member about the possibility of making a return to Nvidia. That meeting took place hours before Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the firm’s earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back. The board voted unanimously to accept his resignation, and won't be backtracking. It's reported that three board members don't agree with that stance, while others have already turned their attention to who will replace Huang long-term. Interim CEO Colette Kress is not being considered as a full-time replacement for Huang.

Recent findings suggest that instead, Arm CEO Rene Haas has appeared as a frontrunner for the top job, with the Nvidia board believed to have already made an approach. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy is also another name under consideration, but the ongoing calls for Huang to be brought back into the fold are thought to have put him off. Rene Haas has reportedly been considere.

It isn't just some of Nvidia's board members who have rallied around Huang. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have also chimed in, while a Taiwanese skyscraper was used to send messages of support to a man who has proven hugely popular in the country.

They ignore troy ounces, treat 14K as 58.5% one day and 58.3% the next, or show a "value" that no buyer will ever pay.

In this tutorial, we'll build a gold value calculator that gets those details right. It runs on plain HTML and JavaScript, updates as the user types, works with a screen reader, keeps its state in a shareable URL and pulls a live spot price through a small Node.js endpoint. The calculation lives in one pure function, so we can test it in a few lines.

Every gold calculator comes down to three inputs: how much the item weighs, how much of that weight is actually gold, and what pure gold is trading for today.

According to recent reports, purity is measured in karats, out of 24. A 14K ring is 14 parts gold and 10 parts other metals, so it's 14 ÷ 24 = 58.3% gold. You'll also see 14K stamped as "585", which is the hallmark many manufacturers use for the same alloy. For a calculator, the karat fraction is the safer default:.

The second detail most tutorials miss is the unit. Gold spot prices are quoted in USD per troy ounce, which is 31.1035 grams, not the 28.35-gram ounce on a kitchen scale. Jewelers also use pennyweight (dwt), which is 1.5552 grams. If your calculator multiplies grams by a per-ounce price without converting, every result is wrong by a factor of 31.

Put together, the formula looks like this:.

For example, with gold at $2,400 per troy ounce, 10 grams of 14K gold contains 5.83 grams of pure gold, which is worth $449.85 at melt.

That $449.85 is the value of the gold content alone. Refiners and buyers pay a percentage of it, because refining, assaying and handling cost money. Depending on the buyer, the item and the market, the payout can sit well below melt value.

Industry observers note that that gap is why good production tools separate the two numbers. A dedicated scrap jewelry gold calculator, like the one The Alloy Market offers, lets sellers estimate what their gold is worth from its weight and karat before they send anything in. Our calculator does the same job with a payout field: leave it at 100% to see melt value, or enter a buyer's rate to see a realistic offer.

Recent findings suggest that start with real form controls and a visible for each one. Placeholder text is not a label: it disappears as soon as the user types, and screen readers handle it inconsistently. The W3C forms tutorial covers the rules in detail.

A few choices here matter more than they look:.

A little CSS gives touch-friendly controls. Keeping inputs at 16px (1rem) also stops iOS Safari from zooming in when a field gets focus.

Sources indicate that the biggest problem with most calculator snippets is that the math is buried inside an event handler, mixed with getElementById calls. You can't test it, and you can't reuse it on a server. Put the calculation and validation in their own module instead:.

It has been revealed that both functions take plain values and return plain values. They don't know a DOM exists, which means the same file can run in the browser, in Node.js and in your test runner.

Industry observers note that notice that we don't round inside the calculation. Rounding happens once, at display time. Rounding in the middle of a chain of multiplications is a classic way to end up a few cents off.

It has been revealed that now connect the form to the module. Listening for the input event on the form itself catches changes from every field, including the dropdowns, so there's no need to wire up each control separately.

With the markup, CSS and script in place, here's the finished calculator showing our 10 g, 14K example with an 80% buyer payout:.

Here's what this code is doing:.

Asking owners to type the spot price works, but prefilling it is friendlier. Don't call a metals price API straight from the browser, though. Your API key would be visible to anyone who opens DevTools, and every visitor would spend one of your API calls.

It has been revealed that instead, put a small endpoint in front of your price provider and cache the result. This example uses Express and the fetch built into Node.js 18 and later:.

Three things keep this endpoint dependable:.

In a recent development, on the page, the loadSpot() function from Step 3 fills the field and shows the time of the price. The field stays editable, so a seller who has a quote from a specific buyer can type that instead.

It has been revealed that A seller comparing offers might want to send their numbers to a family member, or come back to them tomorrow. Because every input has a name, turning the form into a query string is one line with URLSearchParams.

The syncUrl() function in Step 3 runs on every change and uses history.replaceState instead of pushState, so typing doesn't fill the back button with dozens of entries. On load, restoreFromUrl() puts the values back. A link like this opens with the form already filled in:.

This is also the progressive enhancement story. If JavaScript fails to load, the form still submits as a GET request. Your server can read the same parameters, import the same gold.js and render the result in HTML.

Because goldValue() is a pure function, testing it needs no browser and no mocks. Node.js ships with a built-in test runner, so there's nothing to install:.

Run it with node --test. (Add "type": "module" to your package.json so Node treats the files as ES modules.) The troy ounce test is the one worth keeping forever: if anyone "simplifies" the conversion later, it fails immediately.

A quick checklist for putting this calculator on a real store:.

A gold calculator looks like a ten-line script, but the details are what make it useful: converting troy ounces properly, separating melt value from payout, keeping the math testable and making the result accessible and shareable. The same pattern of a pure calculation module, a thin DOM layer and a cached server endpoint works for any calculator where the price depends on several inputs, from shipping estimates to currency conversion.

Mathematically, 14K is 14 ÷ 24 = 58.3%. Many manufacturers stamp 14K jewelry "585" and alloy it to that standard, so both numbers are common. Pick one, state it in the dropdown, and use it consistently.

Let the user choose. Most people weigh jewelry in grams, but spot prices are quoted per troy ounce, so the calculator should accept either and convert internally.

Yes. Drop Step 4 and let users type the spot price, or have a scheduled job write the current price into a static JSON file. Everything else runs entirely in the browser.

Breaking: Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, global OLED monitor shipments doubled year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the latest market research from TrendForce.
  • ASUS maintained its position as the world's largest OLED monitor vendor, accounting for 21.7% of shipments.
  • Price isn't the only obstacle that OLED manufacturers have been addressing, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, global OLED monitor shipments doubled year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the latest market research from TrendForce. Shipments also increased 13% sequentially, reflecting strong demand for OLED displays and improving panel availability. While the market's rapid growth is impressive regardless, there are good reasons why OLED monitors are becoming increasingly popular: they're getting cheaper, better, and considerably easier to justify.

ASUS maintained its position as the world's largest OLED monitor vendor, accounting for 21.7% of shipments. MSI climbed into second place for the first time, capturing 14.5% of the market, while Samsung slipped to third with 11.3%. Both Taiwanese vendors have been particularly aggressive in the gaming monitor market, where increasingly competitive pricing has helped make OLED technology accessible to more buyers, while ubiquitous advertising with tech-conscious gamers has made them highly visible. According to Omdia, mainstream 27-inch QHD 240Hz OLED gaming monitors have seen price cuts exceeding 40% in 2026.

Price isn't the only obstacle that OLED manufacturers have been addressing, though. Earlier generations of OLED monitors had some fairly significant compromises, particularly their relatively limited brightness and unconventional subpixel arrangements that could cause colored fringing around text. Newer tandem OLED panels offer improved brightness and color reproduction, while RGB-stripe OLED layouts bring much cleaner text rendering. These improvements are making OLEDs considerably more attractive as everyday desktop monitors, rather than merely excellent gaming displays with major caveats.

There's also an interesting macroeconomic angle to OLED's growth. The AI industry's insatiable appetite for memory and storage has made upgrading a gaming PC considerably more expensive. DRAM component prices have increased severalfold, while NAND flash and hard drive availability have also been squeezed by demand from AI data centers—though there are early signs of some relief, at least on the flash memory front. Graphics cards, especially (but not exclusively) at the high end, are increasingly difficult to find at anything resembling reasonable prices.

Monitors, meanwhile, aren't directly subject to the same supply pressures affecting DRAM, NAND, and discrete GPUs. That makes upgrading a display an appealing alternative for gamers who aren't particularly interested in spending a small fortune on an entirely upcoming PC. An OLED monitor can substantially improve the gaming experience without requiring a new graphics card, memory kit, or storage drive. The contrast, response times, and color gamut of OLEDs far outstrip even the best LCDs, and that's to say nothing of their superior HDR reproduction thanks to the inherent self-emissive nature of OLED panels.

Industry observers note that with OLED prices falling and the technology's longstanding limitations becoming less noticeable, a fresh monitor is becoming one of the more compelling upgrades available to PC gamers. Indeed, several of our picks for the best gaming monitors, including the best overall, best 4K, and best ultrawide, are based on OLED technology. Though concerns about burn-in and limited lifespan remain, there's no question that OLED is the best display technology we have right now.

#34646. The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2532 w)

The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware company with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.
  • He planned and founded the tech giant in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area.
  • It has been revealed that all this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware company with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.

He planned and founded the tech giant in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area. After more than 30 years, Nvidia had thousands of employees, a global footprint, and a name that people equated to AI chips.

It has been revealed that all this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation. Let’s go back and see how it all began. This is an ongoing saga, so we have listed stories related to the scandal below, which we will upgrade as events unfold.

In a recent development, jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12, after two weeks of news reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with his own subordinate. This is significant for Nvidia, which has had a single CEO since its inception. Huang was the face of the company, and many of its employees, shareholders, partners, and fans still support him despite the circumstances of his departure. He steered Nvidia into the giant that it is today by having the vision to develop CUDA nearly 20 years before ChatGPT made AI accessible to the average user and buying companies that helped it scale deployments to hundreds of thousands of AI GPUs.

By 2022, ChatGPT’s arrival and subsequent boom set the AI race in motion, with tech giants and AI startups buying up as many GPUs as they could get their hands on. The increased demand for Nvidia’s products caused it to break the trillion-dollar mark in less than a year after the release of OpenAI’s LLM. As the largest individual shareholders of the company, Huang and his wife, Lori, became some of the wealthiest people in the world.

Recent findings suggest that the billionaire founder hasn't always gloated about his position. He once remarked in a podcast that if he could turn back time, he wouldn’t have founded Nvidia at all, and also cringed at the praises that the Caltech Board of Trustees chairperson heaped on him before he gave the 2024 keynote speech at the institute’s commencement exercises. He has frequently cited his history working as a “Dishwasher, Busboy, Waiter” at Denny’s, noting it under his experience on his LinkedIn page. More than that, people have seen Jensen go where other celebrity CEOs are rarely seen — enjoying street food in Vietnam, dining at a local fried chicken joint in Korea, and even dragging along 35 of Taiwan’s semiconductor CEOs to a restaurant in Taipei.

Sources indicate that but even as he’s building his “Man of the People” persona, his position as the head of arguably the most notable chipmaker in the AI industry meant that he was also gaining influence in business and governance. Industry leaders noticed the power that Nvidia held over those who want GPUs to train their AI models, with some of his fellow billionaires begging him over dinner to sell them GPUs. Just weeks into President Donald Trump’s second term, Jensen Huang was meeting with him at the White House, discussing AI policy and hardware export controls — something the Biden administration started in 2022 in an attempt to hold back China’s ambition'sin AI.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Industry observers note that the rivalry between the U.S. and China has been simmering for years, with Chinese companies like Huawei getting blacklisted because of their work with the People’s Liberation Army. In August 2022, about three months before ChatGPT made AI a household term, Washington expanded its trade bans on Beijing and imposed export controls on Nvidia’s H100 and A100 GPUs. The company responded to this by building a fresh data center GPU that conformed to U.S. standards specifically for the Chinese market, called the A800, by November of that year. Despite delivering only 70% of the performance of the A100 it was based on, the GPU reportedly still saw great demand from Chinese customers.

However, the A800 only had a relatively short run as the Biden administration once again increased the performance threshold in October 2023, which resulted in the export prohibition of A800 and H800 GPUs to China. This move forced the company to iterate once again, creating latest models that it could sell to Chinese companies, like the Nvidia H20. These chips arrived on the market in early 2024, but before the Biden administration ended in January 2025, it proposed even stricter rules called the AI Diffusion Policy. This sorted nations into different tiers based on trust and risk levels — countries in tier 1, which includes the U.S. and its closest allies, have minimal restrictions, while those in tier 3 are effectively barred from receiving advanced AI GPUs containing U.S. technology.

This is problematic for Nvidia, as China is the second-largest computer market in the world t and represented between 20% and 25% of Nvidia's data center sales. The company lobbied the U.S. government to ease AI GPU export restrictions, with Trump reportedly suspending the proposed Nvidia H20 ban after Jensen spent $1 million to have dinner with the president in early April 2025. The White House went ahead anyway and banned the sale of the AI GPU less than a week after that, resulting in a $5.5 billion write-off for the company.

Jensen Huang himself had harsh comments about Washington’s trade ban, saying that “export control was a failure,” and that it had caused the company’s AI GPU market share in China to go from 95% to zero. He even argued that “conceding an entire market the size of China probably does not make a lot of strategic sense, so I think that has already largely backfired.”.

But even as Huang was fighting to have the trade ban on the Nvidia H20 chip lifted, he continued praising Trump’s tariff plan, calling it “utterly visionary.” The president eventually reversed the ban three months later, and by December 2025, he had approved Nvidia H200 exports to China, but only if Nvidia pays a 25% fee. The newer Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips remain out of reach for Chinese companies, though — at least on paper.

Sources indicate that allegations that Chinese companies have been breaking Washington’s trade ban and smuggling Nvidia AI GPUs into China have been circulating since June 2023, after Reuters revealed that vendors in Shenzhen could secure A100 chips when asked discreetly. They reportedly bought these chips from the excess stocks sold in the open market or through intermediaries in India, Taiwan, and Singapore. Another story published in January 2024 asserted that the Chinese military and related institutions, state-run data centers, and even universities continue buying banned A100 and H100 chips. Six months after that, accounts of underground networks dedicated to smuggling AI GPUs — even entire servers — through other countries started emerging.

In 2025, an investigative report revealed that at least a billion dollars’ worth of Nvidia AI chips were allegedly funneled into China. Some sellers likened the illicit AI GPU trade to a seafood market, with brokers and retailers openly advertising the most advanced Nvidia AI chips online, from RTX 5090 GPUs to complete B200 servers.

Even with all these reports, Huang continued denying that Nvidia’s chips were being smuggled into China. “There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion,” the then-CEO told reporters at Computex 2025. He also added, “The Grace Blackwell system is nearly two tons, and so you’re not going to be shipping — you’re not going to be putting that in your pocket or your backpack anytime soon. And so, these systems are fairly easy to keep track of... but the important thing is that the countries and the companies that we sell to recognize that diversion is not allowed, and everybody would like to continue to buy Nvidia technology, and so they very well monitor themselves very carefully and they’re quite careful about that.”.

Sources indicate that in the midst of all these AI chip smuggling rumors, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency in charge of enforcing U.S. trade sanctions, was found to be “inadequate” and underfunded, and it has been relying on outdated manual processes to enforce restrictions on Chinese tech companies. Despite that, companies and individuals across the world are being investigated and arrested for bypassing Washington’s export controls.

Singaporean authorities broke up a smuggling ring in early 2025 that smuggled Nvidia GPUs for Chinese AI lab DeepSeek, resulting in a raid of 22 different locations and the arrest of nine people. In October of the same year, a Singapore company called Megaspeed, which was led by Alice Huang, allegedly diverted $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Four Americans were then arrested the following month for shipping 400 Nvidia A100s and attempting to send 50 more Nvidia H200 GPUs to China.

An even bigger smuggling scandal unfolded some four months after the arrests, after three Super Micro employees were arrested for smuggling $2.5 billion of Nvidia hardware into China. The suspects included tech giant co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, although Super Micro itself was not implicated. The Super Micro case spanned the globe, with Taiwanese authorities raiding 12 locations related to the case in May 2026, with another nine sites and six people investigated in June. Jensen Huang urged the company to fix its export control compliance after the arrests and raids, telling the media, “We insist our partners are compliant. We hope that they will enhance and improve their regulatory compliance and prevent that from happening in the future.”.

But just five months after he made this statement, one stunning accusation unraveled it all.

Recent findings suggest that on October 29, 2026, The Fresh York Times published a report that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through the executive of a firm who was “close” to him — that executive is Alice Huang. Nvidia denied the accusation. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” a company spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security.".

Industry observers note that but a little over a week later, U.S. intelligence sources claimed that the former Nvidia chief had an affair with the Megaspeed executive. This is the same Megaspeed that has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to the tune of $2 billion. By the evening of Sunday, November 8, Jensen admitted to the affair, although he did not name the third party in his statement.

It has been revealed that many government officials would usually turn a blind eye towards a tech executive’s personal life, but the fact that he is the leader of the U.S.’s premier AI chip maker and that he is also close to the president has caught the attention of authorities. This has led to the U.S. Congress asking him to a closed-door meeting to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and the FBI investigating his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy.

It has been revealed that the admission and allegations led to people digging deeper into Alice Huang. An investigation by The Information revealed that she was connected to a “labyrinth” of companies spanning Singapore, China, and the British Virgin Islands, and that she allegedly helped move around $7.5 billion worth of AI GPU imports. $2 billion was routed from Megaspeed to Speedmatrix, its Malaysia subsidiary, while another $4.6 billion moved directly from the Singaporean company into Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based cloud services company. It has also reportedly bought Nvidia GPUs from other sources, resulting in the estimated total value of its imports.

People close to her also said that she would leverage her relationship with Jensen to customers, often posting pictures with him on her WeChat account, showing potential clients unpublished photos with the Nvidia chief, and even boasting that he would take her to dinner and give her gifts on her birthday. It also seems that Alice Huang was not acting alone. Multiple sources say that Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s husband, was central to the operation to acquire AI GPUs. He even seemingly acknowledged her relationship with Jensen Huang and has jokingly said that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.

However, it seems that the straw that broke the camel’s back was another allegation that Jensen had an affair with another woman — this time, with Kimberly Powell, the tech giant’s vice president of health care who directly reported to him. Hours after this revelation, the company board announced that Jensen had resigned from all his leadership positions at Nvidia, with employees saying he looked “broken and shattered” as he left the company he spent over three decades building in disgrace. Nvidia is looking for internal and external CEO candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive.

According to recent reports, it may be the end of an era, but this does not necessarily spell the end for Jensen Huang. Despite his sudden downfall and quick removal from Nvidia, his status as the king of AI infrastructure remains valuable to the AI industry. Elon Musk even said on X that it “would be an honor” to hire him, and this could ring true for any business that wants to break into the semiconductor space. But does he even want to return?Huang's first public statement after his resignation came on X on Nov. 17, in which the former CEO said he has "outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," and that if asked by the company's board, he would be "honored" to take the job.".

Over 190,000 shareholders, partners, current and former employees, and fans, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have signed an online petition to bring him back as the leader of the manufacturer. President Donald Trump called for his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.The board, however, may not see things the same way.
